raw_final_content:
The target herb has serrate ovate-to-lanceolate leaves or leaflets on a slender partly reddish stem. The most useful feature appears in the third image: a small developing flower head/bud on a thin hairy peduncle, surrounded by several elongated green outer bract-like structures. Together with the paired/opposite-looking, serrate foliage, this points strongly toward Bidens (beggar-ticks / センダングサ属).

Bidens frondosa is my leading species candidate because its heads can show conspicuous leaf-like outer involucral bracts, but the head here is immature and the full leaf architecture is partly obscured. Bidens pilosa and other Bidens remain realistic alternatives. I would therefore record Bidens sp., with B. frondosa as a medium-confidence candidate rather than a confirmed species.

The next decisive evidence would be an open capitulum, a side view of the involucre, a complete leaf showing leaflet number, and especially mature achenes/awns.
